newsitem.title: PANAMA: Hutchison to get Panama ports contract.
newsitem.headline: Hutchison to get Panama ports contract.

text.p: A local unit of Hong Kong-based consortium Hutchison Whampoa Ltd expects to sign a contract to operate Panama's two main ports, a company official said Thursday.

"We expect the contract to be signed within the next month, or before Christmas, with the Panamanian government after Congress approves it," said the official, who declined to be named. "Once signed, we take over operations of the ports on February 1."
Hutchison intended to sign the contract in September but "it was held up due to small technicalities," the official said.

The Hong Kong group made a $22.2-million offer to operate Cristobal Port on the Atlantic Coast and Balboa Port on the Pacific Coast. The two ports, which handle 200,000 and 28,000 containers per year, respectively, are to be turned over to Panama by the United States next year.

Hutchison won a preliminary bidding round in August in an auction that saw foreign investors and diplomats criticize Panama for opening sealed bids and changing regulations in the privatization process.
